career.title: {epithet} {role} of {place}

milestones.name: The Midnight Line
milestones.line: Below this line the sun has never been, and the cable is still paying out.

milestones.name: The Long Snowfall
milestones.line: Snow falls here for weeks before it lands, and it is not snow.

milestones.name: The Plain of Slow Stones
milestones.line: The black stones on this plain grow a few millimetres in a million years.

milestones.name: The Roofs of the Drowned City
milestones.line: You have touched the floor, and it was not the floor.

milestones.name: The Streets Beneath
milestones.line: Under the roofs there are streets, and every one of them runs downhill.

milestones.name: The First Trench
milestones.line: The rock beneath the city splits open, and the sounding lead finds no bottom.

milestones.name: The Second Trench
milestones.line: The floor of the first trench was only the lip of the second.

milestones.name: The Third Trench
milestones.line: Someone has cut soundings into the walls of this trench, and every one is right.

milestones.name: The Seventh Trench
milestones.line: Your chart names this the Seventh Trench, though you have crossed only three.

milestones.name: The Far Shore
milestones.line: There is a beach down here, and the tide is coming in.

milestones.name: The Lantern Grave
milestones.line: Every lantern that ever went out sank this far, and a few are still warm.

milestones.name: The Great Quiet
milestones.line: Nothing here has made a sound since before there were ears to hear one.

milestones.name: The Unbuilt Spires
milestones.line: Towers stand here that no hand built, and they are still rising.

milestones.name: The Bell Below
milestones.line: This is the bell you have heard ringing all along, and it has no rope.

milestones.name: The Lees of Dreaming
milestones.line: The Sleeper's dreams are heavier than water, and this is where they settle.

milestones.name: The Cradle of Tides
milestones.line: The tides are made here, and not by the moon.

milestones.name: The Ocean in the Stone
milestones.line: There is more water held in this stone than in all the seas above it.

milestones.name: The Sleeper's Shadow
milestones.line: You have come this far down and are still standing in its shadow.

milestones.name: The Cable's End
milestones.line: The cable ran out some time ago, and you are still going down.

milestones.name: The Last of the Water
milestones.line: The water thins here, the way air thins near the top of a mountain.

milestones.name: The Space Between Stars
milestones.line: Below the last of the water there are stars, a very long way down.

geography: It knows the names of rivers that no longer run.
It could name every sea, and one more that is on no chart.
It can find its way home from any coast, though it seldom goes.
science: It knows what every element is afraid of.
It names the moons of other worlds as though it had been there.
It measures the world in fathoms and furlongs, and is never wrong.
nature: It calls each creature by its Latin name, and some by older ones.
Animals do not startle when it passes.
It tells one shark from another by the shape of the dark alone.
culture: It can quote from the play that was lost.
It hums along to music from the next room, though there is no next room.
It reads by lantern light, and something reads over its shoulder.
history: It remembers kings their own subjects forgot.
Ask it which ships went down, and it will tell you the tide.
It keeps a list of countries that no longer exist, and the list is growing.
myth: It knows the old gods by their first names.
It could tell you which of the monsters were true.
It reads the tarot before the cards are dealt.
food: It can tell a cheese by the cellar it was aged in.
It has learned every shape that pasta has been asked to take.
It can still name apples that no orchard grows any more.
language: It has a word for the feeling of being watched from below.
It still speaks a little of languages with no one left to answer.
Words come to it in the dark, already spelt.
sport: It remembers who won, long after the crowd has gone home.
It could referee games that nobody has played in a century.
It keeps score even when no one else is playing.
misc: Nothing that washes ashore is a stranger to it.
It knows a little of everything, and a great deal of one thing it will not name.
It can name colours that only appear under water.

geography: It is lost the moment the coast drops out of sight.
Maps unsettle it, as if they might be moving while it sleeps.
science: Numbers make it uneasy, the way deep water does.
It looks up at the night sky and sees only weather.
nature: It names animals the way children do, by noise and colour.
It cannot tell a wolf from a dog in poor light, and here all light is poor.
culture: It leaves the theatre before the second act, every time.
It knows the tune but never the name of the song.
history: To it, everything happened at once, a long time ago.
It mixes up its emperors, and none of them is left to object.
myth: It does not believe in monsters, which suits the monsters.
It calls the old gods by the wrong names, and they answer anyway.
food: It eats without asking what anything is called.
All bread is the same bread to it.
language: It has the words, but not always in the right order.
Old alphabets look to it like weed on a hull.
sport: It has never understood a race, or what it is people are running from.
It cheers at the wrong moment, and the crowd turns to look.
misc: Odd things slip through its fingers, and the tide takes them back.
It walks past the strange shell on the beach without stopping.

fast: It answers before the question has finished rising.
It speaks first and is seldom wrong, which unsettles the ones who wait.
It does not hesitate, and the water barely has time to close.
slow: It waits, and the water waits with it.
It turns each question over twice, like a stone with something under it.
It answers late, as though listening first for another voice.
rare: It says the words the deep keeps for itself.
It reaches past the first answer, and the second, for one that no one else gives.
When it speaks, something far below writes it down.
common: It says what everyone says, and the sea forgives it.
It keeps to the well-lit answers, where the crowd is.
It never strays far from the harbour lights.
night: It comes down after dark, when the lamps are low.
It dives while the house sleeps, and it is not the only one awake.
It keeps late hours, as the deep does.
day: It dives while the world is awake, as if that helps.
It is always back before the house goes quiet.
It likes to descend while there are still people about.
streak: Its lantern has burned for {streak} days without a flicker.
It has come down {streak} days running, and a place is now laid for it.
After {streak} days, the things below have learned when to expect its light.
drifting: It has been away, and the water is letting it go, slowly.
Its cable has gone slack, and the current is carrying it up.
The deep is keeping its place, but not for ever.
newcomer: It is new here, and the deep is patient.
It has only just learned which way is down.
It still smells of the harbour.
warded: Something kept its lantern lit while it slept.
It was absent, and a sign it had earned kept watch in its place.

ward.name: Ward
ward.blurb: Keeps your lantern lit through one missed day, so you do not drift up; you earn one for every seven days in a row and can hold two.

bestiary.name: Lion's Mane Jellyfish
bestiary.line: We followed its tentacles from bow to stern and found no end to them.
bestiary.fact: The largest known jellyfish, and the culprit in the 1926 Sherlock Holmes story 'The Adventure of the Lion's Mane'.

bestiary.name: Portuguese Man o' War
bestiary.line: It came in on the wind under a sail of its own, and the crew stood back from the rail.
bestiary.fact: Not a jellyfish but a colony of zooids that cannot live apart. It cannot swim: its float is a sail, and it goes where the wind sends it.

bestiary.name: Leafy Seadragon
bestiary.line: We took it for a scrap of drifting weed until the weed turned its head.
bestiary.fact: Found only off southern Australia. Its leafy lobes are for hiding, not swimming, and the male carries the eggs on his tail until they hatch.

bestiary.name: Ocean Sunfish
bestiary.line: It lay on its side in the swell, taking the sun, and watched us with no interest at all.
bestiary.fact: Its name, Mola, is Latin for millstone. It basks on its side at the surface, where seabirds pick parasites from its skin.

bestiary.name: Barreleye
bestiary.line: It looked up at us through its own head.
bestiary.fact: Its head is a clear, fluid-filled dome. The dark spots on its face are nostrils; its real eyes, with green lenses, turn within to look up or ahead.

bestiary.name: Vampire Squid
bestiary.line: It drew its cloak up over itself and showed us only the soft spines inside.
bestiary.fact: Neither squid nor octopus, it is the last of its order. It eats marine snow, gathered on two long threads and wrapped in mucus.

bestiary.name: Hatchetfish
bestiary.line: It was thin and bright as a coin, and it lit itself so as not to be seen.
bestiary.fact: Lights on its belly match the faint light from above, hiding its outline from hunters below. It can dim or brighten them to suit.

bestiary.name: Giant Siphonophore
bestiary.line: It passed the porthole for seven minutes, and we never saw either end.
bestiary.fact: It can reach 40 m, longer than a blue whale, yet it is a colony of thousands of zooids on a single stem. It lures prey with blue light.

bestiary.name: Black Seadevil
bestiary.line: We watched a small light for some time before we saw what was holding it.
bestiary.fact: Only the female has a lure, lit by bacteria that live in it. The tiny males do not fuse to her as some anglerfish do; they hold on only briefly.

bestiary.name: Gulper Eel
bestiary.line: Its mouth unfolded like a net, wider than the whole of the rest of it.
bestiary.fact: Its mouth is far larger than its body, yet it mostly eats small crustaceans. The tip of its whip-like tail glows pink, with the odd red flash.

bestiary.name: Colossal Squid
bestiary.line: Its eye was wider than our porthole, and for a moment the two were level.
bestiary.fact: The heaviest invertebrate known, with the largest eyes of any animal, about 27 cm across. No one filmed one alive in the deep until 2025.

bestiary.name: Fangtooth
bestiary.line: It was small enough to hold in one hand, and it seemed to be mostly teeth.
bestiary.fact: For its size it has the largest teeth of any fish in the sea. Its two longest fangs slide into sockets beside its brain when it shuts its mouth.

bestiary.name: Dumbo Octopus
bestiary.line: It rowed past on two small fins like ears, and did not look our way.
bestiary.fact: The deepest-dwelling octopus known: one was filmed at 6,957 m in the Java Trench. It swims with the two ear-like fins above its eyes.

bestiary.name: Tripod Fish
bestiary.line: It stood on three thin stilts above the ooze and faced the current like a sentry.
bestiary.fact: It perches on three fin rays up to a metre long, facing the current to catch what drifts past. Each one is both male and female.

bestiary.name: Sea Pig
bestiary.line: A herd of them crossed the plain below us, grazing, and none of them looked up.
bestiary.fact: A sea cucumber that walks on leg-like tube feet, pumped up with water. Herds of hundreds roam the abyssal plain, eating fresh scraps in the mud.

bestiary.name: Xenophyophore
bestiary.line: A crumbling stone on the floor turned out to be alive, and to be a single cell.
bestiary.fact: A single cell up to 20 cm across that builds a fragile shell from grains of mud. Its name means 'bearer of foreign bodies'.

bestiary.name: Mariana Snailfish
bestiary.line: It was small and pale and nearly clear, and it was not troubled by any of this.
bestiary.fact: It lives deeper than almost any other fish, down to about 8,000 m. Its bones, even its skull, are not fully hardened.

bestiary.name: Supergiant Amphipod
bestiary.line: Its cousins in the rock pools fit on a fingernail; this one was as long as a forearm.
bestiary.fact: The largest amphipod known, it grows to about 34 cm, longer than a school ruler. Few have ever come up in a baited trap.

bestiary.name: Swimming Sea Cucumber
bestiary.line: It lifted off the mud like a veil of pink glass, swam a little way, and came down again.
bestiary.fact: Its genus name, Enypniastes, means 'dreamer'. If something touches it, its fragile skin can slough off in a glowing cloud.

bestiary.name: Deep One
bestiary.line: It stood upright at the edge of the lamp, which nothing down here has any reason to do.
bestiary.fact: The log records it seven times, always at the same depth and each time a little nearer the lamp. It has never been seen to swim.

bestiary.name: Father Dagon
bestiary.line: A hill we had charted rose a little in the night, and was a hill again by morning.
bestiary.fact: The city's carvings call him father, and never say of what. In the oldest carvings he is smaller.

bestiary.name: Mother Hydra
bestiary.line: We heard her as a slow chorus of breathing, no two breaths quite in time.
bestiary.fact: No carving in the city shows her whole. Each shows a different part, and no two of the parts agree.

bestiary.name: Shoggoth
bestiary.line: It learned the shape of our sphere on a single pass, and wore it for a while.
bestiary.fact: It has no shape of its own, only borrowed ones, and some of the shapes it borrows belong to nothing still alive.

bestiary.name: The Dreamer
bestiary.line: What we took for a ridge of pale rock closed, very slowly, like a hand.
bestiary.fact: Its glyph means 'the one who dreams'. In all the city's writing there is no glyph for waking.
